name: Sarah M. London

career.title: Director of Special Projects (after stints in the Los Angeles film industry and Harvard fundraising)
Vice President, Client Management and Operations; then Chief Product Officer
SVP, Technology and Modernization; then EVP, Advanced Technology and President, Health Care Enterprises

background_rationale: Built her career in healthcare data analytics and technology, as chief product officer at Optum Analytics, a health-tech venture investor and Centene's head of technology modernization before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Centene withdrew its 2025 financial guidance after finding a sharp shift in morbidity among its ACA Marketplace members, then took corrective pricing actions for 2026 in states covering 95% of Marketplace membership.

In the 2026 proxy statement, London said Centene had completed 12 divestitures, including Magellan Health, Magellan Rx and PANTHERx, and made difficult decisions where programs no longer met its risk and return thresholds.

Reporting second-quarter results, London called the improved full-year outlook a meaningful milestone on Centene's path to restoring profitability, as it raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to more than $4.80.
Centene named former Lincoln Financial CFO Chris Neczypor as its next chief financial officer, effective Jan. 1, 2027, succeeding Drew Asher.

personal_story.hook: Sarah London worked in the Los Angeles film industry before building a career in health data and becoming Centene's CEO.
personal_story.summary: London grew up in St. Louis and studied history and literature at Harvard, where she played Division I tennis. After college she spent two years in the film industry in Los Angeles, then returned to Boston to do fundraising at Harvard focused on health, education and equity, and worked for the nonprofit Health Leads. After earning her MBA at Chicago Booth in 2010, she moved into healthcare analytics at Humedica and Optum, rising to chief product officer before investing in health startups at Optum Ventures. She joined Centene in 2020 to lead technology modernization and was named CEO in March 2022, at the time among the youngest CEOs in the Fortune 500.
